iast: dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre samavetā yuyutsavaḥ · māmakāḥ pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya
meaning: Dhritarashtra said: On the field of dharma, at Kurukshetra, my sons and the sons of Pandu have gathered, eager to fight. What did they do, Sanjaya?
lifeNote: The Gita opens with a worried question from someone who cannot see for himself. Many of our anxieties start the same way: wanting to know an outcome we cannot control.
actions: Write down one question that is worrying you today, and next to it what you can actually control.
Before asking someone for news today, notice whether you are asking out of care or out of fear.
Spend five minutes today on the task in front of you instead of guessing how things will turn out.

iast: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṁ vyūḍhaṁ duryodhanastadā · ācāryamupasaṅgamya rājā vacanamabravīt
meaning: Sanjaya said: Seeing the Pandava army drawn up in battle formation, King Duryodhana went to his teacher Drona and spoke these words.
lifeNote: When we feel threatened, our first move is often to look for reassurance. Notice who you run to, and why.
actions: When something unsettles you today, wait two minutes before you go to someone about it.
Name one person you turn to when you are anxious, and thank them this week.
Notice one moment today when you seek reassurance, and ask yourself what you are really afraid of.

iast: paśyaitāṁ pāṇḍuputrāṇāmācārya mahatīṁ camūm · vyūḍhāṁ drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā
meaning: Look, teacher, at this mighty army of the sons of Pandu, arranged for battle by your own gifted disciple, the son of Drupada.
lifeNote: Duryodhana's words carry a hidden complaint: you trained the man now facing us. Watch for blame tucked inside your words when you are afraid.
actions: Reread one message before you send it today and remove any hidden blame.
If you feel let down by someone, say it plainly once instead of hinting at it.
Notice one time today when fear makes you look for someone to blame.

iast: atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi · yuyudhāno virāṭaśca drupadaśca mahārathaḥ
meaning: Here are heroes and mighty archers, equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, a great chariot-warrior.
lifeNote: Fear makes us count the other side's strengths over and over. Counting your own steadies you more.
actions: List three strengths you bring to a challenge you are facing.
When you catch yourself comparing with a rival today, switch to one thing you can improve.
Ask a friend what they think you are good at, and believe them.

iast: dhṛṣṭaketuścekitānaḥ kāśirājaśca vīryavān · purujitkuntibhojaśca śaibyaśca narapuṅgavaḥ
meaning: There are Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the finest of men.
lifeNote: Every name in this list is someone's story. The people around you each carry a whole life you only glimpse.
actions: Learn one new thing about a colleague or classmate today.
Use someone's name warmly when you greet them today.
Write down the names of three people who stood by you this year.

iast: yudhāmanyuśca vikrānta uttamaujāśca vīryavān · saubhadro draupadeyāśca sarva eva mahārathāḥ
meaning: There are mighty Yudhamanyu and valiant Uttamauja, the son of Subhadra, and the sons of Draupadi, all of them great chariot-warriors.
lifeNote: Even young Abhimanyu stands among the great warriors. Courage does not wait for age or permission.
actions: Do one thing today that you have been waiting to feel ready for.
Encourage a younger person in your life to try something bold.
Speak up once today in a place where you usually stay quiet.

sanskrit: अस्माकं तु विशिष्टा ये तान्निबोध द्विजोत्तम ।
नायका मम सैन्यस्य संज्ञार्थं तान्ब्रवीमि ते ॥
iast: asmākaṁ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama · nāyakā mama sainyasya saṁjñārthaṁ tānbravīmi te
meaning: Now hear, best of the twice-born, about the distinguished ones on our side, the leaders of my army. I name them for you.
lifeNote: After listing the enemy's heroes, Duryodhana turns to his own to calm himself. It is fine to remind yourself of your support, as long as it is not only to quiet fear.
actions: Name three people or resources you can rely on for a current challenge.
When anxious, write down what is on your side before what is against you.
Reach out to one supporter today just to say you appreciate them.

iast: bhavānbhīṣmaśca karṇaśca kṛpaśca samitiñjayaḥ · aśvatthāmā vikarṇaśca saumadattistathaiva ca
meaning: There is you yourself, Bhishma, Karna, and Kripa, who is victorious in battle; Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and the son of Somadatta too.
lifeNote: Duryodhana names his teacher first, partly to flatter him. Notice when you praise someone to get something rather than because you mean it.
actions: Give one honest compliment today with nothing expected back.
Notice one moment when you flatter someone, and say something true instead.
Thank a teacher or mentor for one specific thing they taught you.

sanskrit: अन्ये च बहवः शूरा मदर्थे त्यक्तजीविताः ।
iast: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ · nānāśastrapraharaṇāḥ sarve yuddhaviśāradāḥ
meaning: And many other heroes are ready to give up their lives for my sake, armed with many kinds of weapons and all skilled in war.
lifeNote: Others' loyalty is a gift, not something we are owed. Treat the people who back you with care.
words: ready to give up their lives
actions: Thank someone who has made a sacrifice for you.
Ask yourself whether you are asking too much of someone close to you, and ease off if so.
Do one small thing today for a person who always shows up for you.

iast: aparyāptaṁ tadasmākaṁ balaṁ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam · paryāptaṁ tvidameteṣāṁ balaṁ bhīmābhirakṣitam
meaning: Our army, guarded by Bhishma, is beyond measure, while theirs, guarded by Bhima, is limited. (The words can also be read the other way: ours is not enough, theirs is ample, which shows Duryodhana's doubt.)
lifeNote: The same words can sound like confidence or like worry. Pay attention to the doubt behind your own bold statements.
actions: When you say "it will be fine" today, pause and check whether you believe it.
Write down one fear you have been covering with confidence.
Share an honest doubt with someone you trust.

iast: ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgamavasthitāḥ · bhīṣmamevābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi
meaning: So all of you, standing firm at your assigned posts at every point of entry, must protect Bhishma above all.
lifeNote: Every team needs each person to hold their own place. Doing your part well protects everyone.
actions: Do your own part of a group task really well today without being asked.
Ask your team or family what they most need from you this week.
Finish one task you committed to before starting something new.

iast: tasya saṁjanayanharṣaṁ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ · siṁhanādaṁ vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṁ dadhmau pratāpavān
meaning: Then the grandsire Bhishma, the valiant elder of the Kurus, roared like a lion and blew his conch loudly, to cheer Duryodhana.
lifeNote: Bhishma sees Duryodhana's fear and answers with encouragement. Sometimes the kindest thing is to lift someone's spirits before the hard part begins.
actions: Send a word of encouragement to someone facing something hard this week.
Start one task today with a deliberate, confident first step.
Cheer someone on today, even for a small win.

iast: tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bheryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ · sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumulo'bhavat
meaning: Then conches, kettledrums, tabors, drums and horns all blared out at once, and the sound was tremendous.
lifeNote: Noise can carry us along before we have thought anything through. Find a quiet moment before you join in.
actions: Take five minutes of silence before an important decision today.
Turn off notifications for one hour today.
When a group gets heated today, take one breath before you respond.

iast: tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau · mādhavaḥ pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ
meaning: Then Krishna and Arjuna, seated in a great chariot yoked to white horses, blew their divine conches.
lifeNote: Krishna and Arjuna answer the noise with clear, steady sound. You can meet chaos calmly instead of adding to it.
actions: Answer one tense situation today in a calm, clear voice.
Choose one clear message you want to get across this week and say it simply.
Before a meeting or class, sit quietly for a minute to steady yourself.

iast: pāñcajanyaṁ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṁ dhanaṁjayaḥ · pauṇḍraṁ dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṁ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ
meaning: Krishna blew the conch Panchajanya, Arjuna blew Devadatta, and Bhima, doer of mighty deeds, blew the great conch Paundra.
lifeNote: Each warrior has his own conch and his own voice. Your contribution does not have to sound like anyone else's.
actions: Share one idea today in your own words, even if it is different.
Notice one strength of yours that others do not have.
Stop comparing your progress with one particular person for a day.

iast: anantavijayaṁ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ · nakulaḥ sahadevaśca sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau
meaning: King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughosha and Manipushpaka.
lifeNote: The brothers stand together, each sounding his own note. Family and friends are strongest when each one shows up.
actions: Call a sibling or close friend just to check in.
Join one family or team activity today with full attention.
Remind someone close that you have their back.

iast: kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ · dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ
meaning: The king of Kashi, a superb archer, the great chariot-warrior Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata, and the unconquered Satyaki,
lifeNote: Allies of every kind join the cause. Good work usually needs many different people.
actions: Ask someone with a different skill to help you with a task.
Thank one person whose quiet help you usually overlook.
Include someone new in a plan this week.

iast: drupado draupadeyāśca sarvaśaḥ pṛthivīpate · saubhadraśca mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛthakpṛthak
meaning: Drupada, the sons of Draupadi, and the mighty-armed son of Subhadra, O king, each blew his own conch.
lifeNote: Everyone sounds their own conch, yet it is one army. You can keep your own voice and still belong to something larger.
actions: Contribute one idea to a group effort today.
Notice a team you belong to and the part you play in it.
Help a group goal today even if it is not your own task.

iast: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṁ hṛdayāni vyadārayat · nabhaśca pṛthivīṁ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan
meaning: That tremendous uproar, echoing through sky and earth, shattered the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.
lifeNote: A guilty conscience hears every sound as a threat. Acting rightly lets you meet challenges without dread.
actions: Set right one small thing you have been feeling uneasy about.
Apologise for something you have been avoiding.
Notice what makes you feel uneasy today and ask what it is pointing to.

iast: atha vyavasthitān dṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrānkapidhvajaḥ · pravṛtte śastrasaṁpāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ
meaning: Then, seeing Dhritarashtra's sons drawn up for battle as weapons were about to fly, Arjuna, whose banner bore Hanuman, raised his bow.
lifeNote: Arjuna is ready at the start. Readiness on the outside can hide questions on the inside, and that is human.
actions: Before starting a big task today, ask yourself one honest question about it.
Prepare for one challenge this week, and leave room for doubt.
Notice when you are acting confident while feeling unsure.

iast: hṛṣīkeśaṁ tadā vākyamidamāha mahīpate · senayorubhayormadhye rathaṁ sthāpaya me'cyuta
meaning: He said these words to Krishna, O king: Achyuta, place my chariot between the two armies.
lifeNote: Arjuna wants to see clearly before he acts. Stepping back to the middle gives you a view of both sides.
actions: Before you decide something today, try to see it from the other side.
Stand back from one conflict and describe it in neutral words.
Ask a trusted person to help you see a situation clearly.

iast: yāvadetānnirīkṣe'haṁ yoddhukāmānavasthitān · kairmayā saha yoddhavyamasminraṇasamudyame
meaning: so that I may look at those standing here eager for war, and see whom I must fight in this battle.
lifeNote: Knowing exactly what you face is the first step to facing it well.
actions: Write down exactly what you are up against in one current problem.
Look straight at one task you have been avoiding and list its parts.
Name one fear clearly instead of letting it stay vague.

iast: yotsyamānānavekṣe'haṁ ya ete'tra samāgatāḥ · dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ
meaning: I want to see those who have come here to fight, wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra in this war.
lifeNote: People sometimes go along with what is wrong to please someone powerful. Check whose approval drives your choices.
actions: Notice one choice today that you are making only to please someone.
Say no once to a request that goes against your values.
Ask yourself whose approval matters most to you, and whether it should.

iast: evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata · senayorubhayormadhye sthāpayitvā rathottamam
meaning: Sanjaya said: Addressed in this way by Arjuna, O Bharata, Krishna drew up that finest chariot between the two armies,
lifeNote: Krishna does what Arjuna asks, without argument. A good guide lets you see for yourself first.
words: by Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep
actions: Let someone you are guiding discover one thing for themselves.
Listen fully to a request before you respond to it.
Help a friend do what they asked, without adding advice.

iast: bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṁ ca mahīkṣitām · uvāca pārtha paśyaitānsamavetānkurūniti
meaning: facing Bhishma, Drona and all the rulers of the earth, and said: Arjuna, look at all these Kurus gathered here.
lifeNote: Krishna stops the chariot in front of the people Arjuna loves most. Hard truths often stand right in front of us.
words: in front of Bhishma and Drona
actions: Look honestly at one relationship that is difficult right now.
Have one conversation you have been postponing.
Write down what you really feel about a hard situation.

iast: tatrāpaśyatsthitānpārthaḥ pitṛnatha pitāmahān · ācāryānmātulānbhrātṛnputrānpautrānsakhīṁstathā
meaning: There Arjuna saw standing fathers and grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends,
lifeNote: The enemy suddenly has familiar faces. Conflicts feel very different once we see the people in them.
actions: Think of someone you are in conflict with and name one good thing about them.
Remember a person you once disagreed with who also helped you.
Before criticising someone today, picture them as a person with a family.

iast: śvaśurānsuhṛdaścaiva senayorubhayorapi · tānsamīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvānbandhūnavasthitān
meaning: fathers-in-law and well-wishers in both armies. Seeing all these kinsmen standing ready, Arjuna, the son of Kunti,
lifeNote: Love does not take sides neatly. It is normal to care about people on both sides of a conflict.
actions: If you are caught between two people, tell each of them you care.
Accept one mixed feeling today without forcing it to make sense.
Write to someone you have drifted from because of a disagreement.

iast: kṛpayā parayā''viṣṭo viṣīdannidamabravīt · dṛṣṭvemaṁ svajanaṁ kṛṣṇa yuyutsuṁ samupasthitam
meaning: was overcome with deep pity and said in sorrow: Krishna, seeing my own people gathered here eager to fight,
lifeNote: Compassion is good, but here it slides into despair. Feeling deeply is human; letting it freeze you is what the Gita will address.
actions: Name one feeling that is weighing on you right now.
Let yourself feel a sad moment today without rushing to fix it.
Talk to someone you trust about something that has been heavy.

sanskrit: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति ।
iast: sīdanti mama gātrāṇi mukhaṁ ca pariśuṣyati · vepathuśca śarīre me romaharṣaśca jāyate
meaning: my limbs give way, my mouth is dry, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
lifeNote: Anxiety lives in the body: dry mouth, shaky hands, racing heart. Noticing these signs is the first step to calming them.
actions: When you feel anxious today, slow your breathing: in for four counts, out for six.
Notice where stress shows up in your body and relax that spot.
Drink a glass of water and take three slow breaths before a stressful task.

sanskrit: न च शक्नोम्यवस्थातुं भ्रमतीव च मे मनः ॥
iast: gāṇḍīvaṁ sraṁsate hastāttvakcaiva paridahyate · na ca śaknomyavasthātuṁ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ
meaning: The Gandiva bow slips from my hand, my skin is burning, I cannot stand steady, and my mind seems to be spinning.
lifeNote: Even the greatest archer drops his bow when his mind spins. Overwhelm happens to the strongest, and it can pass.
actions: If you feel overwhelmed today, sit down and do one tiny task.
Put your feet flat on the floor and notice five things you can see.
Write down everything on your mind, then pick just one thing.

iast: nimittāni ca paśyāmi viparītāni keśava · na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave
meaning: I see bad omens, Krishna, and I can see no good in killing my own people in battle.
lifeNote: When we are afraid, everything looks like a bad sign. Check whether you are seeing facts or fear.
actions: Take one worry today and write down the facts separately from the fears.
When you see a "sign" that things will go wrong, look for one sign that they might go right.
Ask a friend to give you an honest view of a situation that scares you.

sanskrit: न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च ।
किं नो राज्येन गोविन्द किं भोगैर्जीवितेन वा ॥
iast: na kāṅkṣe vijayaṁ kṛṣṇa na ca rājyaṁ sukhāni ca · kiṁ no rājyena govinda kiṁ bhogairjīvitena vā
meaning: I do not want victory, Krishna, nor a kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is a kingdom to us, Govinda, or enjoyment, or even life?
lifeNote: When grief strikes, everything we wanted can suddenly feel empty. That feeling is real, and it is also not the whole truth.
actions: If something you wanted feels pointless today, ask what deeper need it was meant to meet.
Do one small thing that usually brings you joy, even if you do not feel like it.
Write down one reason you still have for showing up tomorrow.

sanskrit: येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च ।
त इमेऽवस्थिता युद्धे प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा धनानि च ॥
iast: yeṣāmarthe kāṅkṣitaṁ no rājyaṁ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca · ta ime'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṁstyaktvā dhanāni ca
meaning: The very people for whose sake we want kingdom, enjoyment and pleasure stand here in battle, ready to give up their lives and wealth.
lifeNote: We often work for the people we love, then lose them in the chase. Keep the reason in sight, not just the goal.
actions: Spend unhurried time today with someone you work hard for.
Write down who you are really working for, and call one of them.
Skip one unnecessary task today to be present with family.

iast: ācāryāḥ pitaraḥ putrāstathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ · mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ śyālāḥ sambandhinastathā
meaning: Teachers, fathers, sons and grandfathers, uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law and other relatives.
lifeNote: Arjuna lists everyone because each relationship matters. Take stock of the people who shaped you.
actions: Write down three relatives who shaped you, and one thing each gave you.
Call an elder in your family this week.
Share a family memory with someone younger.

sanskrit: अपि त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्य हेतोः किं नु महीकृते ॥
iast: etānna hantumicchāmi ghnato'pi madhusūdana · api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kiṁ nu mahīkṛte
meaning: I do not wish to kill them, Madhusudana, even if they kill me; not even for rule over the three worlds, let alone this earth.
lifeNote: Some things are not worth winning at the cost of the people involved. Know what you will not trade.
words: for rule over the three worlds
actions: Write down one thing you would not give up for any amount of success.
Let go of winning one small argument today.
Choose a relationship over being right once this week.

iast: nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ kā prītiḥ syājjanārdana · pāpamevāśrayedasmānhatvaitānātatāyinaḥ
meaning: What joy could we have from killing the sons of Dhritarashtra, Janardana? Only sin would cling to us for killing these aggressors.
lifeNote: Getting even rarely brings the joy we imagine. Ask what you will feel after, not just in the moment.
actions: When you want to get back at someone today, picture how you will feel tomorrow.
Let one small grudge go this week.
Replace one sharp reply with silence today.

sanskrit: स्वजनं हि कथं हत्वा सुखिनः स्याम माधव ॥
iast: tasmānnārhā vayaṁ hantuṁ dhārtarāṣṭrānsvabāndhavān · svajanaṁ hi kathaṁ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava
meaning: So it is not right for us to kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our own kin. How could we be happy after killing our own people, Krishna?
lifeNote: Arjuna's love is real, but he is using it to escape a duty. Good feelings can still lead to poor choices.
actions: Notice one time today when a kind-sounding reason is really an excuse.
Ask yourself whether you are avoiding a hard duty, and what it costs.
Talk through a hard choice with someone wise before deciding.

iast: yadyapyete na paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ · kulakṣayakṛtaṁ doṣaṁ mitradrohe ca pātakam
meaning: Even if they, their minds clouded by greed, see nothing wrong in destroying a family or sin in betraying friends,
lifeNote: Greed blinds people to harm they would otherwise see. Check where wanting more is clouding your view.
actions: Notice one thing you want badly and ask what it might be costing you.
Pause before a purchase today and ask if you really need it.
Check one decision for whether greed or fear is driving it.

iast: kathaṁ na jñeyamasmābhiḥ pāpādasmānnivartitum · kulakṣayakṛtaṁ doṣaṁ prapaśyadbhirjanārdana
meaning: why should we, who clearly see the wrong in destroying a family, not know to turn away from this sin, Janardana?
lifeNote: Others' wrongs do not excuse ours. Hold your own standard even when others drop theirs.
actions: Keep one promise today even though someone else broke theirs.
Do the right thing in one small situation where no one is watching.
Write down one value you will hold to regardless of others.

iast: kulakṣaye praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ · dharme naṣṭe kulaṁ kṛtsnamadharmo'bhibhavatyuta
meaning: When a family is destroyed, its age-old traditions are lost; and when tradition is lost, lawlessness overtakes the whole family.
lifeNote: Shared values hold families and communities together. Look after the good traditions you have inherited.
actions: Keep one good family tradition alive this week.
Teach a younger person something your elders taught you.
Write down one value your family stands for.

iast: adharmābhibhavātkṛṣṇa praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ · strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ
meaning: When lawlessness prevails, Krishna, the women of the family are led astray, and from that comes confusion in the social order. (This is Arjuna's worry, voicing the views of his time.)
lifeNote: Arjuna is piling up reasons for what he already wants to do. Notice when your mind lines up arguments to defend a feeling.
actions: When you catch yourself listing reasons for something today, ask what you already decided.
Argue the other side of one of your strong opinions for two minutes.
Notice one fear about the future and check how likely it really is.

iast: saṅkaro narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṁ kulasya ca · patanti pitaro hyeṣāṁ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ
meaning: Such confusion leads both the family and its destroyers to hell, and their ancestors fall too, deprived of the ritual offerings of food and water.
lifeNote: Arjuna's thinking now spirals into worst cases. When worry snowballs, come back to the present step.
words: for the destroyers of the family
deprived of offerings of food and water
actions: When a worry spirals today, stop and name the next single step.
Write the worst case down, then the most likely case beside it.
Honour an ancestor or elder today with a small act of remembrance.

iast: doṣairetaiḥ kulaghnānāṁ varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ · utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāśca śāśvatāḥ
meaning: Through these wrongs of those who destroy families and cause social confusion, the timeless duties of community and family are ruined.
lifeNote: Our actions ripple into families and communities. Think about who your choices will touch.
words: of the destroyers of the family
actions: Before a big decision this week, list who else it will affect.
Do one thing today that strengthens your community.
Ask an elder what they hope you will carry forward.

iast: utsannakuladharmāṇāṁ manuṣyāṇāṁ janārdana · narake'niyataṁ vāso bhavatītyanuśuśruma
meaning: We have heard, Janardana, that people whose family duties are destroyed live in hell indefinitely.
lifeNote: "We have heard" — Arjuna leans on hearsay to support his fear. Check where your beliefs come from.
actions: Check the source of one thing you believe before you repeat it.
Ask "how do I know this?" about one worry today.
Read one reliable source on something you have only heard about.

sanskrit: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् ।
iast: aho bata mahatpāpaṁ kartuṁ vyavasitā vayam · yadrājyasukhalobhena hantuṁ svajanamudyatāḥ
meaning: Alas! What a great sin we are set on committing, ready to kill our own people out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.
lifeNote: Arjuna now judges himself harshly. Guilt can help us reflect, but not when it becomes a reason to give up.
words: out of greed for kingdom and pleasure
actions: Replace one harsh thought about yourself today with a fair one.
If you feel guilty about something, take one step to set it right.
Talk to yourself today the way you would talk to a friend.

iast: yadi māmapratīkāramaśastraṁ śastrapāṇayaḥ · dhārtarāṣṭrā raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṁ bhavet
meaning: It would be better for me if the sons of Dhritarashtra, weapons in hand, killed me in battle while I stood unarmed and did not resist.
lifeNote: Giving up can feel like the noble choice when we are overwhelmed. Often it is just exhaustion speaking.
actions: If you feel like giving up today, rest first and decide tomorrow.
Ask for help with one thing that feels too heavy to carry alone.
Do one small next step instead of deciding the whole future.

iast: evamuktvā'rjunaḥ saṁkhye rathopastha upāviśat · visṛjya saśaraṁ cāpaṁ śokasaṁvignamānasaḥ
meaning: Sanjaya said: Having spoken like this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
lifeNote: The Gita begins with a hero who has fallen apart. You do not need to have it all together to begin learning.
actions: Admit one thing you are struggling with to someone you trust.
Let today be a day to rest if you need it, and plan one step for tomorrow.
Remember that starting from a low point is still starting.

iast: taṁ tathā kṛpayā'viṣṭamaśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam · viṣīdantamidaṁ vākyamuvāca madhusūdanaḥ
meaning: Sanjaya said: To Arjuna, overcome with pity, his troubled eyes full of tears and his heart sinking, Krishna spoke these words.
lifeNote: Krishna does not ignore Arjuna's tears, and he does not drown in them either. Being with someone in pain is the first step to helping them.
words: eyes full of tears and troubled
actions: Sit with someone who is sad today without rushing to fix it.
Let yourself cry or feel low without judging it.
Ask a struggling friend what would help, then listen.

iast: kutastvā kaśmalamidaṁ viṣame samupasthitam · anāryajuṣṭamasvargyamakīrtikaramarjuna
meaning: The Lord said: Where has this weakness come from, Arjuna, at such a critical time? It does not suit a noble person; it leads neither to heaven nor to honour.
lifeNote: Sometimes kindness sounds like a firm question: is this really you? A good friend reminds you of who you are.
actions: Ask yourself honestly: is this fear really me, or just a passing mood?
Remind a friend of a time they were strong.
Write down one quality you want to live up to today.

sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते ।
iast: klaibyaṁ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitattvayyupapadyate · kṣudraṁ hṛdayadaurbalyaṁ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa
meaning: Do not give in to faint-heartedness, Arjuna; it does not suit you. Shake off this petty weakness of heart and stand up, conqueror of enemies.
lifeNote: "Stand up" is one of the Gita's great calls. You do not need to feel brave to take the next step.
actions: Do the one thing today that you have been too discouraged to start.
When you feel small, stand up straight and take three deep breaths.
Say out loud: I can take the next step.

sanskrit: कथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन ।
iast: kathaṁ bhīṣmamahaṁ saṁkhye droṇaṁ ca madhusūdana · iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāvarisūdana
meaning: Arjuna said: How can I fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle, Krishna? They deserve my reverence.
lifeNote: Respect for elders is good, but it should not stop you from doing what is right. You can honour someone and still disagree.
actions: Disagree respectfully with someone you look up to, once this week.
Thank an elder for something even if you see things differently.
Write down one value you hold that differs from your family's, and why.

iast: gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvān · śreyo bhoktuṁ bhaikṣyamapīha loke · hatvārthakāmāṁstu gurūnihaiva · bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān
meaning: It would be better to live in this world on alms than to kill these noble teachers. Even if they seek gain, killing them would leave every pleasure stained with their blood.
lifeNote: Arjuna's heart is in the right place, but grief is choosing for him. Wait until the storm passes before making big choices.
actions: Delay one big decision until you are calmer.
Write down what you would choose if you were not afraid.
Talk to a mentor before deciding something that weighs on you.

sanskrit: यद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः ।
iast: na caitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo · yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ · yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāma · ste'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
meaning: We do not know which is better for us, to conquer them or to be conquered. Those whose deaths would leave us not wanting to live, the sons of Dhritarashtra, stand before us.
lifeNote: Admitting "I don't know" is where wisdom begins. Confusion said out loud is easier to work through.
actions: Say "I don't know yet" once today instead of pretending.
List the pros and cons of a choice you are stuck on.
Ask someone wiser what they would do in your place.

iast: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ · pṛcchāmi tvāṁ dharmasaṁmūḍhacetāḥ · yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṁ brūhi tanme · śiṣyaste'haṁ śādhi māṁ tvāṁ prapannam
meaning: My nature is overcome by weakness and I am confused about my duty. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your disciple; teach me, for I have come to you for refuge.
lifeNote: The turning point of the Gita is a request for help. Asking to be taught is a strength, not a defeat.
actions: Ask someone to teach you something you are struggling with.
Admit to one person today that you need guidance.
Find a mentor or teacher for one area of your life.

iast: na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyā · dyacchokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām · avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddham · rājyaṁ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam
meaning: I cannot see what would take away this grief that dries up my senses, even if I gained an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth, or even rule over the gods.
lifeNote: No outside success can heal an inner wound. Some pain needs understanding, not more achievement.
actions: Notice one thing you hope a future success will fix, and ask if it really would.
Spend time today on inner peace rather than outer progress.
Write down what you are really grieving right now.

sanskrit: न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
iast: evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaṁ guḍākeśaḥ parantapa · na yotsya iti govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṁ babhūva ha
meaning: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Krishna, Arjuna, the conqueror of sleep, said "I will not fight" and fell silent.
lifeNote: Sometimes we say a firm "no" just to stop the discomfort. Silence after that can be the start of listening.
actions: After saying no to something today, sit quietly and ask why.
Take five minutes of silence before replying to a hard message.
Notice one refusal of yours that came from fear.

iast: tamuvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasanniva bhārata · senayorubhayormadhye viṣīdantamidaṁ vacaḥ
meaning: Then, O king, between the two armies, Krishna, as if smiling, spoke these words to the grieving Arjuna.
lifeNote: Krishna smiles, not to mock, but because he can see the way through. A calm presence can lighten someone's heaviest moment.
actions: Bring a calm, warm presence to someone who is upset today.
Smile at a problem today before you start solving it.
Remember a time a crisis looked smaller later.

iast: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṁ prajñāvādāṁśca bhāṣase · gatāsūnagatāsūṁśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
meaning: The Lord said: You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words that sound wise. The wise grieve neither for the dead nor for the living.
lifeNote: Krishna's teaching starts here: much of our sorrow comes from not seeing the whole picture.
words: those not to be grieved for
actions: Look at one sorrow from a wider view: how will it look in a year?
Notice when you sound wise but feel lost, and be honest about it.
Read or listen to something that widens your view today.

sanskrit: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः ।
न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
iast: na tvevāhaṁ jātu nāsaṁ na tvaṁ neme janādhipāḥ · na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
meaning: There was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor these kings; and never in the future shall any of us cease to be.
lifeNote: Who you truly are does not begin or end with this moment. That can make today's fears feel smaller.
actions: When something feels like the end today, remember you have been through endings before.
Spend a few minutes reflecting on what in you stays constant.
Write a letter to your future self.

iast: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṁ yauvanaṁ jarā · tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati
meaning: Just as the soul passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes into another body. The steady person is not confused by this.
lifeNote: You have already changed many times: the child you were is gone, yet you are still you. Change is not the same as loss.
actions: Look at an old photo of yourself and notice what is still the same.
Accept one change in your life today without resisting it.
Tell someone how you have grown in the past five years.

iast: mātrā-sparśās tu kaunteya śītoṣṇa-sukha-duḥkha-dāḥ · āgamāpāyino 'nityās tāṁs titikṣasva bhārata
meaning: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go; they do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
lifeNote: A hard day, a harsh comment, a delayed result — all of it passes. Let it move through you without letting it decide who you are.
actions: When something upsets you today, pause and say to yourself: this too will pass.
Notice one discomfort today and simply watch it change without reacting.
Write down one worry from last month that no longer matters.

sanskrit: यं हि न व्यथयन्त्येते पुरुषं पुरुषर्षभ ।
iast: yaṁ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṁ puruṣarṣabha · samaduḥkhasukhaṁ dhīraṁ so'mṛtatvāya kalpate
meaning: The steady person whom these do not disturb, who stays the same in pain and pleasure, O best of men, is fit for immortality.
lifeNote: Steadiness is not coldness. It is feeling everything without being thrown by it.
actions: Respond to one good and one bad moment today with the same calm.
When you get good news today, enjoy it without clinging.
When you get bad news, wait ten minutes before reacting.

sanskrit: नासतो विद्यते भावो नाभावो विद्यते सतः ।
iast: nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ · ubhayorapi dṛṣṭo'ntastvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ
meaning: The unreal has no lasting existence, and the real never ceases to be. Those who see the truth have understood the nature of both.
lifeNote: Moods, opinions and trends come and go. Build your life on what lasts: values, love, truth.
actions: List three things in your life that will still matter in ten years.
Spend one hour today on something lasting instead of something passing.
Notice one trend you follow and ask if it is real or temporary.

sanskrit: अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ।
iast: avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṁ tatam · vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścit kartumarhati
meaning: Know that what pervades this whole universe is indestructible. No one can destroy that which is imperishable.
lifeNote: There is something in you that no failure, insult or loss can touch.
actions: After a setback today, say: this does not touch who I really am.
Write down one inner quality nobody can take from you.
Sit quietly for five minutes and notice the awareness behind your thoughts.

iast: antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ · anāśino'prameyasya tasmādyudhyasva bhārata
meaning: These bodies of the eternal, indestructible and immeasurable soul are said to come to an end. Therefore fight, Arjuna.
lifeNote: Because the body is temporary, use it well while you have it. Act fully now.
actions: Do one thing today you would regret not doing.
Take care of your body today so it can carry your purpose.
Stop postponing one meaningful task.

sanskrit: य एनं वेत्ति हन्तारं यश्चैनं मन्यते हतम् ।
उभौ तौ न विजानीतो नायं हन्ति न हन्यते ॥
iast: ya enaṁ vetti hantāraṁ yaścainaṁ manyate hatam · ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṁ hanti na hanyate
meaning: One who thinks the soul is a killer, and one who thinks it is killed, both fail to understand. The soul neither kills nor is killed.
lifeNote: We often mistake the surface of things for their reality. Look deeper before you judge.
actions: Before judging someone today, look for what you cannot see.
Notice one assumption you make about a person, and question it.
Read about a belief different from yours with an open mind.

sanskrit: न्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
iast: na jāyate mriyate vā kadāci · nnāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ · ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṁ purāṇo · na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
meaning: The soul is never born and never dies. It did not come into being and will not cease to be. Unborn, eternal, everlasting and ancient, it is not killed when the body is killed.
lifeNote: Grief for those we lose is natural. This verse offers a quiet comfort: the deepest part of them is not gone.
actions: Remember someone you have lost and one thing they gave you that lives on.
Light a lamp or say a prayer for someone who has passed.
Share a happy memory of a loved one with family.

sanskrit: कथं स पुरुषः पार्थ कं घातयति हन्ति कम् ॥
iast: vedāvināśinaṁ nityaṁ ya enamajamavyayam · kathaṁ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṁ ghātayati hanti kam
meaning: One who knows the soul to be indestructible, eternal, unborn and unchanging — how can that person kill anyone, Arjuna, or cause anyone to be killed?
lifeNote: Seeing the deeper self in everyone changes how we treat them.
actions: Treat one difficult person today as someone with the same inner worth as you.
Pause before an unkind word and remember who you are speaking to.
Do one kind act for a stranger.

iast: vāsāṁsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya · navāni gṛhṇāti naro'parāṇi · tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇā · nyanyāni saṁyāti navāni dehī
meaning: Just as a person throws off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the soul casts off worn-out bodies and enters new ones.
lifeNote: Endings can be like changing clothes. Something old falls away so something new can begin.
actions: Let go of one old habit that no longer fits you.
Clear out something you have outgrown and give it away.
Welcome one new beginning in your life today.

sanskrit: नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः ।
न चैनं क्लेदयन्त्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः ॥
iast: nainaṁ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṁ dahati pāvakaḥ · na cainaṁ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
meaning: Weapons cannot cut the soul, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, and wind cannot dry it.
lifeNote: Whatever happens around you, your deepest self stays untouched. Let that steady you.
actions: In a stressful moment today, remind yourself: this cannot reach the real me.
Write down one hardship you came through that did not break you.
Repeat this verse slowly once before sleep.

iast: acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca · nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo'yaṁ sanātanaḥ
meaning: The soul cannot be cut, burned, wetted or dried. It is eternal, present everywhere, stable, unmoving and ancient.
lifeNote: Like a mountain in weather, there is a steady part of you beneath every mood.
actions: Sit still for five minutes and feel the steadiness under your thoughts.
When a mood swings today, name it and let it pass.
Find a quiet place today and stay there a few minutes.

iast: avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate · tasmādevaṁ viditvainaṁ nānuśocitumarhasi
meaning: The soul is said to be unseen, beyond thought and unchanging. Knowing it to be so, you should not grieve.
lifeNote: Some things cannot be grasped by thinking alone. Let quiet understanding comfort you.
actions: Spend five minutes today just being, not thinking or doing.
Accept one thing you cannot fully understand right now.
Comfort a grieving friend with presence rather than explanations.

sanskrit: अथ चैनं नित्यजातं नित्यं वा मन्यसे मृतम् ।
iast: atha cainaṁ nityajātaṁ nityaṁ vā manyase mṛtam · tathāpi tvaṁ mahābāho naivaṁ śocitumarhasi
meaning: And even if you think the soul is constantly born and constantly dies, even then, mighty-armed one, you should not grieve.
lifeNote: Krishna meets Arjuna where he is: even if you do not accept the deeper view, grief need not consume you.
actions: Look at one sorrow from two different viewpoints today.
Let one sadness be there without letting it run your whole day.
Do one practical thing today even while you are grieving.

sanskrit: जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युर्ध्रुवं जन्म मृतस्य च ।
iast: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṁ janma mṛtasya ca · tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṁ śocitumarhasi
meaning: Death is certain for one who is born, and birth is certain for one who dies. So you should not grieve over what cannot be avoided.
lifeNote: Accepting what cannot be changed frees your energy for what can.
actions: Write down one thing you cannot change and one thing you can.
Stop fighting one fact of life today and work with it instead.
Spend time today with someone who is aging, and listen to them.

iast: avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata · avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā
meaning: Beings are unseen before birth, seen in the middle, and unseen again after death, Arjuna. What is there to lament in that?
lifeNote: Life is a short visible stretch between two mysteries. Make the middle count.
actions: Do one thing today that you want your life to be remembered for.
Write down how you want to spend the "visible middle" of your life.
Let one small worry go by seeing how short life is.

iast: āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidena · māścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ · āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti · śrutvāpyenaṁ veda na caiva kaścit
meaning: Some see the soul as a wonder, some speak of it as a wonder, some hear of it as a wonder; yet even after hearing, no one truly understands it.
lifeNote: Keep a sense of wonder. Not everything needs to be fully figured out to be meaningful.
actions: Look at the sky, a tree or a child today with fresh wonder.
Ask one big question today and enjoy not knowing the answer.
Read something about the universe that amazes you.

iast: dehī nityamavadhyo'yaṁ dehe sarvasya bhārata · tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṁ śocitumarhasi
meaning: The soul that lives in every body can never be killed, Arjuna. So you should not grieve for any being.
lifeNote: The same life lives in everyone. Treat all beings with that respect.
actions: Be kind to an animal or plant today.
Notice the same spark of life in someone you dislike.
Do one act of care for a being that cannot thank you.

iast: svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi · dharmyāddhi yuddhācchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate
meaning: Considering your own duty, too, you should not waver. For a warrior there is nothing better than a battle fought for what is right.
lifeNote: Your role brings real responsibilities. When the cause is just, stand firm in it.
actions: Write down your main responsibilities right now and do one of them well.
Stand up for something fair today, even in a small way.
Stop wavering on one decision you already know is right.

iast: yadṛcchayā copapannaṁ svargadvāramapāvṛtam · sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam
meaning: Fortunate are the warriors, Arjuna, who get such a battle; it comes unsought, like an open door to heaven.
lifeNote: Some challenges are opportunities in disguise. The hard thing in front of you may be the door you needed.
actions: Name one current challenge and one opportunity hidden inside it.
Say yes to one hard opportunity you would usually avoid.
Thank a difficulty that made you stronger.

sanskrit: अथ चेत्त्वमिमं धर्म्यं संग्रामं न करिष्यसि ।
ततः स्वधर्मं कीर्तिं च हित्वा पापमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast: atha cettvamimaṁ dharmyaṁ saṁgrāmaṁ na kariṣyasi · tataḥ svadharmaṁ kīrtiṁ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi
meaning: But if you do not fight this righteous battle, you will abandon your duty and your honour, and you will incur sin.
lifeNote: Avoiding a responsibility is also a choice, and it has consequences too.
actions: Name one duty you have been avoiding and take the first step.
Notice the cost of not acting on something important.
Keep one commitment today even though it is uncomfortable.

iast: akīrtiṁ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te'vyayām · saṁbhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate
meaning: People will speak of your disgrace for ever, and for an honoured person, disgrace is worse than death.
lifeNote: Your name is built by your actions over time. Protect it by doing right, not by worrying about gossip.
actions: Do one thing today that matches the person you want to be known as.
Keep your word in one small matter today.
Let go of worry about what people say and focus on what you do.

sanskrit: येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम् ॥
iast: bhayādraṇāduparataṁ maṁsyante tvāṁ mahārathāḥ · yeṣāṁ ca tvaṁ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
meaning: The great warriors will think you withdrew from battle out of fear, and those who held you in high regard will think little of you.
lifeNote: Others may misread your choices. Make sure your own reasons are ones you respect.
actions: Check one choice today: is it fear or wisdom?
Explain your reasons honestly to someone who matters to you.
Do one brave thing today that you have been avoiding out of fear.

sanskrit: निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम् ॥
iast: avācyavādāṁśca bahūn vadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ · nindantastava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim
meaning: Your enemies will say many cruel things, mocking your strength. What could be more painful than that?
lifeNote: Fear of criticism is real, but it should not be the main reason you act. Do what is right; let the critics talk.
actions: Let one unfair comment pass today without arguing.
Do one thing you believe in even if someone may mock it.
Write down a criticism that hurt you and what you learned from it.

sanskrit: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम् ।
iast: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm · tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
meaning: If you are killed you will reach heaven; if you win you will enjoy the earth. So rise, Arjuna, resolved to fight.
lifeNote: When you act rightly, every outcome has value. That makes it easier to commit fully.
actions: Commit to one task today and decide that both success and failure will teach you.
Stand up and start something you have been weighing for too long.
Write down what you gain even if a current effort fails.

iast: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau · tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpamavāpsyasi
meaning: Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, and engage in the battle. That way you will not incur sin.
lifeNote: Do the work for its own sake. Results will come and go; your steadiness stays.
actions: Before a test or meeting today, decide to give your best whatever the result.
Treat one win and one setback today with the same calm.
Write "effort, not outcome" somewhere you will see it.

sanskrit: एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां शृणु ।
iast: eṣā te'bhihitā sāṁkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṁ śṛṇu · buddhyāyukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṁ prahāsyasi
meaning: I have explained this to you through knowledge. Now hear it through the practice of yoga: with this understanding you will break free from the bondage of action.
lifeNote: Understanding is the first step; practice makes it real. Knowing and doing go together.
actions: Take one idea you agree with and practise it today.
Turn one thing you learned this week into a small habit.
Teach someone a lesson by doing it, not by explaining it.

iast: nehābhikramanāśo'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate · svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
meaning: On this path no effort is ever wasted and there is no harm. Even a little of this practice protects you from great fear.
lifeNote: Small steps count. Even five minutes of practice today is not wasted.
actions: Do just five minutes of something good for you today.
Restart a habit you dropped, without guilt.
Notice one small effort that made a difference this week.

iast: vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana · bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo'vyavasāyinām
meaning: The resolute mind is single-pointed, Arjuna. The thoughts of the irresolute branch out endlessly in many directions.
lifeNote: A scattered mind tires itself out. Pick one direction and give it your full attention.
actions: Choose one priority for today and finish it before anything else.
Close every tab and app except the one you need for an hour.
Write down your main goal for this week in one sentence.

iast: yāmimāṁ puṣpitāṁ vācaṁ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ · vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ
meaning: The unwise speak flowery words, Arjuna. They delight in the letter of the Vedas and claim there is nothing beyond it.
lifeNote: Fancy words can hide shallow ideas. Look for the meaning, not the decoration.
words: attached to the letter of the Vedas
actions: When something sounds too good today, ask what it actually means.
Say one thing today in the simplest words you can.
Notice an advertisement and see what it is really selling.

iast: kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām · kriyāviśeṣabahulāṁ bhogaiśvaryagatiṁ prati
meaning: Full of desires and set on heaven, they recommend many special rituals aimed at pleasure and power, which lead only to rebirth as the fruit of action.
lifeNote: Even good practices can turn into a way of getting things. Notice why you do what you do.
words: giving birth as the fruit of action
the path to pleasure and power
actions: Do one good deed today with no reward in mind.
Look at one habit and ask whether it is for growth or for show.
Pray or reflect today without asking for anything.

iast: bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṁ tayāpahṛtacetasām · vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
meaning: Those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away by such talk, cannot develop the steady understanding needed for deep meditation.
lifeNote: A mind always chasing more cannot settle. Wanting less makes room for peace.
words: of those attached to pleasure and power
actions: Skip one purchase or indulgence today and notice how you feel.
Spend ten minutes in quiet without your phone.
List three things you already have that are enough.

iast: trai-guṇya-viṣayā vedā nistrai-guṇyo bhavārjuna · nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kṣema ātmavān
meaning: The Vedas deal with the three qualities of nature. Rise above them, Arjuna: be free from opposites, steady in goodness, free from worry about gain and keeping, and centred in the Self.
lifeNote: Most stress comes from chasing and guarding. Spend one part of your day neither chasing nor guarding anything.
actions: Take ten minutes today where you want nothing from anyone.
When you feel pulled between two extremes, choose the calm middle once today.
Before sleeping, list one thing you did without expecting anything back.

iast: yāvān artha uda-pāne sarvataḥ samplutodake · tāvān sarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
meaning: A small well is of little use where water floods everywhere. In the same way, for one who truly knows, the rituals of the Vedas serve only as much purpose.
lifeNote: When you understand why you do something, you need fewer rules to keep doing it.
actions: Pick one habit and write down why it matters to you.
Drop one rule you follow only out of fear today.
Explain to someone the real purpose behind your work.

iast: karmaṇy evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana · mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi
meaning: You have a right to your actions, but never to their results. Do not let results be your motive, and do not cling to inaction.
lifeNote: Do your best on the task in front of you, then let the outcome be what it is. Worry about results is what scatters focus.
actions: Finish one task today without checking how it was received until evening.
Prepare fully for one thing today, then stop and rest.
Do one kind act today that no one will know about.

sanskrit: योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय ।
सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते ॥
iast: yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya · siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga ucyate
meaning: Perform your duty steadfast in yoga, Arjuna, giving up attachment, and being even-minded in success and failure. Such evenness of mind is called yoga.
lifeNote: Treat a win and a loss with the same calm today. Evenness is a skill you can practise.
actions: After any result today, good or bad, take three slow breaths before reacting.
Do one task with full care and no thought of praise.
Tell a friend about a failure as calmly as you would a success.

iast: dūreṇa hy avaraṁ karma buddhi-yogād dhanañjaya · buddhau śaraṇam anviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ
meaning: Action driven by desire is far lower than action guided by wisdom. Take refuge in wisdom, Arjuna; those who act only for results are to be pitied.
lifeNote: Before acting today, ask: is this coming from clear thinking or from craving the result?
actions: Pause before one decision today and name the reason behind it.
Choose the wise option over the quick win once today.
Write the one thing you would do even if no one rewarded you.

iast: buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte · tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
meaning: One who is joined with wisdom lets go of both good and bad results here. So devote yourself to yoga; yoga is skill in action.
lifeNote: Skill in action means doing the work well and lightly at the same time.
actions: Do one routine task today with full attention, as if it were your craft.
Improve one small thing in how you work today.
Finish one task and let it go without replaying it.

sanskrit: कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः ।
iast: karmajaṁ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṁ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ · janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṁ gacchantyanāmayam
meaning: The wise, joined to this understanding, give up the fruits of their actions. Freed from the bondage of birth, they reach the state beyond all suffering.
lifeNote: Letting go of results is not giving up. It is the freedom to act without fear.
words: freed from the bondage of birth
actions: Finish one task today and let go of how it is received.
Send off one piece of work without checking for reactions.
Notice the relief of doing something just because it is right.

sanskrit: तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥
iast: yadā te mohakalilaṁ buddhirvyatitariṣyati · tadā gantāsi nirvedaṁ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
meaning: When your understanding crosses beyond the mire of delusion, you will become indifferent to all that you have heard and all that is yet to be heard.
lifeNote: When you see clearly, you stop needing every opinion. Trust what you have understood.
words: to what is yet to be heard
actions: Avoid one round of advice-seeking today and trust your own judgement.
Mute one noisy source of opinions for a day.
Write down one thing you are clear about.

iast: śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā · samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi
meaning: When your mind, now confused by conflicting teachings, stands unmoving and steady in meditation, then you will attain yoga.
lifeNote: Too many voices can confuse. A steady mind finds its own still point.
actions: Sit in silence for ten minutes today.
Pick one teacher or method and stick to it for a week.
When advice conflicts, pause and listen to your calmer inner voice.

sanskrit: स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम् ॥
iast: sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava · sthitadhīḥ kiṁ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, how would you describe a person of steady wisdom, settled in meditation? How does such a person speak, sit and walk?
lifeNote: Arjuna wants to know how wisdom looks in daily life. It shows in how you talk, rest and move.
actions: Notice how you speak when you are stressed, and slow it down.
Walk somewhere today without rushing.
Watch someone calm and learn one habit from them.

sanskrit: प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान् ।
iast: prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha manogatān · ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate
meaning: The Lord said: When a person gives up all the desires that arise in the mind and is content in the Self, by the Self, that person is called one of steady wisdom.
lifeNote: Real contentment comes from inside, not from getting what you want.
actions: Find one moment of contentment today that needs nothing new.
Let one craving pass without acting on it.
End the day by naming three things that were enough.

iast: duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ · vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate
meaning: One whose mind is not shaken by sorrow, who does not crave pleasure, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.
lifeNote: Attachment, fear and anger often travel together. Loosen one and the others weaken.
words: free from attachment, fear and anger
actions: When you feel angry today, look for the fear underneath it.
Let go of one small attachment today.
Stay calm through one setback and notice how it feels.

sanskrit: नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast: yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham · nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
meaning: One who is unattached everywhere, who neither rejoices at the good nor hates the bad that comes, is established in wisdom.
lifeNote: Good and bad days both pass. Meeting each without clinging or resisting is real strength.
actions: Notice one good thing today and enjoy it lightly.
Meet one bad thing today without complaining.
End the day with "this too was part of it".

iast: yadā saṁharate cāyaṁ kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ · indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
meaning: When a person can withdraw the senses from their objects completely, as a tortoise draws in its limbs, that person's wisdom is firmly established.
lifeNote: Like a tortoise, you can pull back from distractions when you need to. Practise turning inward on purpose.
actions: Put your phone in another room for one hour of study or work.
Close your eyes for two minutes and let the outside world fade.
Choose one distraction to avoid completely today.

iast: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ · rasavarjaṁ raso'pyasya paraṁ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
meaning: Sense objects fall away from one who abstains from them, but the taste for them remains. Even that taste falls away when one has seen the Supreme.
lifeNote: Avoiding a temptation helps, but the craving fades only when you find something deeper.
actions: Replace one unhelpful habit with something meaningful today.
When a craving comes, spend five minutes on something you love instead.
Write down what you are really looking for behind one craving.

iast: yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ · indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṁ manaḥ
meaning: Even the mind of a wise person who is trying hard, Arjuna, can be carried away by force by the turbulent senses.
lifeNote: Slipping up does not mean you are weak. Even the wise struggle; keep going.
actions: If you slipped up on a goal recently, start again today without guilt.
Plan one guardrail for a habit you keep breaking.
Be gentle with yourself about one mistake.

sanskrit: तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः ।
वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता ॥
iast: tāni sarvāṇi saṁyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ · vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
meaning: Restraining all the senses, one should sit disciplined, with the mind fixed on me. One whose senses are under control has steady wisdom.
lifeNote: Discipline is easier with something higher to focus on. Give your attention a worthy home.
actions: Begin your work today with a minute of focus on why it matters.
Keep one simple discipline today: sleep, food or screen time.
Sit still for five minutes with your attention on one thought.

iast: dhyāyato viṣayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣūpajāyate · saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho 'bhijāyate
meaning: Dwelling on objects of the senses breeds attachment. From attachment comes desire, and from desire comes anger.
lifeNote: Anger often starts as a thought you kept returning to. Catch the thought early.
actions: When a thought keeps returning today, name it and gently turn away once.
Notice one craving today and wait ten minutes before acting on it.
Before reacting in anger, trace it back to what you wanted.

iast: krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛti-vibhramaḥ · smṛti-bhraṁśād buddhi-nāśo buddhi-nāśāt praṇaśyati
meaning: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confused memory; from confused memory, the loss of reason; and with reason lost, one is ruined.
lifeNote: Words said in anger are the hardest to take back. A pause protects your judgement.
actions: If you feel anger rising today, wait one full minute before speaking.
Apologise for one thing said in haste recently.
Drink a glass of water and breathe before replying to a heated message.

iast: rāgadveṣaviyuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran · ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati
meaning: A self-disciplined person who moves among sense objects with senses under control, free from attraction and aversion, attains serenity.
lifeNote: You do not have to run from the world. Engage with it without being pulled around by likes and dislikes.
actions: Do one task today that you dislike, calmly and well.
Enjoy one pleasure today without wanting more of it.
Notice one strong like or dislike and hold it lightly.

iast: prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṁ hānirasyopajāyate · prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
meaning: In that serenity all sorrows come to an end. For one whose mind is calm, understanding soon becomes steady.
lifeNote: A calm mind thinks better. Settle first, then decide.
actions: Take five slow breaths before your next important decision.
Start your study or work session with two minutes of calm.
When upset today, calm down before you reply.

iast: nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā · na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
meaning: The undisciplined have no wisdom and no focus. Without focus there is no peace, and without peace, where is happiness?
lifeNote: Happiness grows from peace, and peace from a focused mind. Start with focus.
actions: Do one thing at a time today, fully.
Set aside a quiet time each day this week.
Notice what disturbs your peace most and reduce it.

iast: indriyāṇāṁ hi caratāṁ yanmano'nuvidhīyate · tadasya harati prajñāṁ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi
meaning: When the mind follows the wandering senses, it carries away one's wisdom, as the wind carries away a boat on the water.
lifeNote: A drifting mind is like a boat without a rudder. Keep a hand on the steering.
actions: When your mind drifts today, gently bring it back to the task.
Notice what pulls your attention most and limit it for a day.
Set a clear intention before you open your phone.

iast: tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ · indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
meaning: Therefore, mighty-armed one, one whose senses are fully restrained from their objects has firmly established wisdom.
lifeNote: Self-control is not punishment; it is choosing where your energy goes.
actions: Choose one thing to say no to today so you can say yes to something better.
Keep one promise to yourself today.
Notice an urge and wait ten minutes before acting on it.

sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी ।
यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
iast: yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti saṁyamī · yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
meaning: What is night for all beings is when the self-controlled person is awake; and what is day for all beings is night for the sage who sees.
lifeNote: The wise are awake to what others miss, and unmoved by what excites everyone. You can live differently from the crowd.
actions: Do one thing today that matters to you even if no one else cares about it.
Skip one popular distraction and spend that time on growth.
Wake up ten minutes earlier for quiet reflection.

iast: āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṁ · samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat · tadvatkāmā yaṁ praviśanti sarve · sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī
meaning: Just as rivers flow into the ocean, which is ever being filled yet stays still, so the person into whom all desires flow without disturbance attains peace, not the one who chases desires.
lifeNote: Be like the ocean: let wants come and go without flooding you.
actions: When a desire comes today, notice it like a wave and let it pass.
Sit by water or picture the ocean for two minutes.
Go one day without buying anything you do not need.

iast: vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṁścarati niḥspṛhaḥ · nirmamo nirahaṁkāraḥ sa śāṁtimadhigacchati
meaning: A person who gives up all desires and lives free from longing, without possessiveness and without ego, attains peace.
lifeNote: "Mine" and "me" are heavy words. Holding them more lightly brings peace.
actions: Share or lend something you are possessive about.
Let someone else take credit for something today.
Notice how often you say "my" today and soften it once.

sanskrit: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति ।
iast: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati · sthitvā'syāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati
meaning: This is the divine state, Arjuna. Having reached it, one is never deluded again. Established in it even at the end of life, one attains the peace of Brahman.
lifeNote: Chapter 2 ends with a promise: steady wisdom is possible, and it lasts. Every step towards it counts.
actions: Review what you learned from Chapter 2 and pick one teaching to live this week.
Write down one way you have become steadier recently.
Share one verse that helped you with someone you love.

sanskrit: तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
iast: jyāyasī cetkarmaṇaste matā buddhirjanārdana · tatkiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśava
meaning: Arjuna said: Krishna, if you think knowledge is better than action, why are you urging me to do this terrible deed?
lifeNote: Arjuna hopes understanding will excuse him from acting. Insight is meant to guide action, not replace it.
actions: Turn one idea you have been thinking about into a first action today.
Notice when "I need to think more" is really avoidance.
Ask a clear question when advice seems to contradict itself.

iast: vyāmiśreṇeva vākyena buddhiṁ mohayasīva me · tadekaṁ vada niścitya yena śreyo'hamāpnuyām
meaning: Your words seem mixed and they confuse my mind. Tell me clearly the one path by which I can reach the highest good.
lifeNote: When you are confused, ask for one clear next step, not a whole map.
actions: Ask someone for the single most important thing you should do next.
Reduce one confusing choice to the one option that matters most.
Write your problem in one sentence.

iast: loke'smindvividhā niṣṭhā purā proktā mayānagha · jñānayogena sāṁkhyānāṁ karmayogena yoginām
meaning: The Lord said: In this world there are two paths, as I taught long ago, sinless one: the path of knowledge for the contemplative, and the path of action for the active.
lifeNote: People find their way differently: some through thinking, some through doing. Respect your own nature.
actions: Notice whether you learn better by reflecting or by doing, and lean into it.
Respect someone today whose path is different from yours.
Try the other path once: reflect if you usually act, act if you usually reflect.

iast: na karmaṇāmanārambhānnaiṣkarmyaṁ puruṣo'śnute · na ca saṁnyasanādeva siddhiṁ samadhigacchati
meaning: One does not reach freedom from action by not acting, nor does one reach perfection by renunciation alone.
lifeNote: Avoiding work does not bring peace. Peace comes from how you work.
actions: Start one task you have been putting off.
Do your work today with a calm, unhurried attitude.
Notice that resting after real effort feels better than avoiding effort.

iast: na hi kaścitkṣaṇamapi jātu tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt · kāryate hyavaśaḥ karma sarvaḥ prakṛtijairguṇaiḥ
meaning: No one can remain without action even for a moment. Everyone is made to act, helplessly, by the qualities born of nature.
lifeNote: You are always doing something, even when you think you are not. Choose your actions on purpose.
actions: Notice one thing you do automatically today, and do it on purpose instead.
Plan your evening instead of drifting through it.
Replace one idle habit with a chosen action.

sanskrit: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।
iast: karmendriyāṇi saṁyamya ya āste manasā smaran · indriyārthānvimūḍhātmā mithyācāraḥ sa ucyate
meaning: One who restrains the organs of action but sits dwelling on sense objects in the mind is deluded and called a hypocrite.
lifeNote: Outer discipline with inner craving is just pretending. Work on the mind, not only the behaviour.
actions: Notice one thing you avoid outwardly but dwell on inwardly.
Be honest with yourself about one craving today.
Replace one forced rule with a gentler habit you can actually keep.

iast: yastvindriyāṇi manasā niyamyārabhate'rjuna · karmendriyaiḥ karmayogamasaktaḥ sa viśiṣyate
meaning: But one who controls the senses with the mind and, without attachment, engages the organs of action in the yoga of action, excels, Arjuna.
lifeNote: The best path is engaged, focused and unattached: fully in the work, light about the results.
actions: Give full attention to one task today and let go of how it turns out.
Help someone today without expecting thanks.
Before starting work, set your intention, then focus on the work alone.

sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।
iast: niyataṁ kuru karma tvaṁ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ · śarīrayātrāpi ca te na prasiddhyedakarmaṇaḥ
meaning: Do your duty, for action is better than inaction. Without action you could not even keep your body alive.
lifeNote: Doing your daily duties well is already spiritual practice.
actions: Finish your most important duty of the day before anything else.
Do a routine chore with care and attention.
Write down three duties you have and do one of them really well.

iast: yajñārthātkarmaṇo'nyatra loko'yaṁ karmabandhanaḥ · tadarthaṁ karma kaunteya muktasaṁgaḥ samācara
meaning: Action done for any purpose other than as an offering binds a person to this world. So, Arjuna, do your work as an offering, free from attachment.
lifeNote: Work done as an offering feels lighter. Dedicate your effort to something larger than yourself.
actions: Dedicate one task today to someone you love or to the greater good.
Before starting work, say a short prayer or intention.
Do one job today for the benefit of others, not your own credit.

iast: sahayajñāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā purovāca prajāpatiḥ · anena prasaviṣyadhvameṣa vo'stviṣṭakāmadhuk
meaning: In the beginning the Creator brought forth beings together with sacrifice and said: By this you shall prosper; let this be the cow that grants all you wish for.
lifeNote: Giving is built into life. When you contribute, you also grow.
actions: Give something today: time, help or a kind word.
Volunteer for a small task that helps a group.
Notice how giving makes you feel, and write it down.

iast: devānbhāvayatānena te devā bhāvayantu vaḥ · parasparaṁ bhāvayantaḥ śreyaḥ paramavāpsyatha
meaning: Nourish the gods with this, and may the gods nourish you. By nourishing one another, you will all reach the highest good.
lifeNote: Life works through mutual care. Support others, and you will find support.
actions: Help someone who has helped you, without being asked.
Thank the people whose work makes your day possible.
Do one thing today that benefits your neighbourhood.

sanskrit: तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
iast: iṣṭānbhogānhi vo devā dāsyante yajñabhāvitāḥ · tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
meaning: Nourished by sacrifice, the gods will give you the enjoyments you desire. One who enjoys their gifts without offering anything back is simply a thief.
lifeNote: Taking without giving back is a quiet kind of theft. Return something for what you receive.
actions: Give back to one person or place that gives to you.
Before a meal, take a moment to be grateful.
Return a favour you have been meaning to repay.

sanskrit: भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
iast: yajñaśiṣṭāśinaḥ santo mucyante sarvakilbiṣaiḥ · bhuñjate te tvaghaṁ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt
meaning: The good, who eat what remains after an offering, are freed from all wrongs. But those who cook only for themselves eat sin.
lifeNote: Sharing turns ordinary things into something sacred. Share before you consume.
words: who eat what remains of sacrifice
actions: Share a meal or snack with someone today.
Offer food to someone in need this week.
Say a word of thanks before eating.

iast: annādbhavanti bhūtāni parjanyādannasambhavaḥ · yajñādbhavati parjanyo yajñaḥ karmasamudbhavaḥ
meaning: Beings come from food, food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice is born of action.
lifeNote: Everything is connected. Your actions feed into a cycle much larger than you.
actions: Trace where one meal came from and thank everyone in the chain.
Avoid wasting food today.
Do one thing today that cares for nature.

iast: karma brahmodbhavaṁ viddhi brahmākṣarasamudbhavam · tasmātsarvagataṁ brahma nityaṁ yajñe pratiṣṭhitam
meaning: Know that action comes from the Vedas, and the Vedas from the Imperishable. So the all-pervading Brahman is always present in sacrifice.
lifeNote: When you work as an offering, you touch something sacred in the ordinary.
words: the Vedas arising from the Imperishable
actions: Do one ordinary task today as if it were sacred.
Begin your day with a short moment of gratitude.
Find meaning in one small duty today.

iast: evaṁ pravartitaṁ cakraṁ nānuvartayatīha yaḥ · aghāyurindriyārāmo moghaṁ pārtha sa jīvati
meaning: One who does not help turn this wheel that has been set in motion, living only for sense pleasure, lives in vain, Arjuna.
lifeNote: A life lived only for yourself feels empty in the end. Play your part in the larger cycle.
actions: Do one thing today purely for someone else's benefit.
Notice one way you only take, and find a way to give back.
Ask yourself what you are contributing to the world this week.

sanskrit: आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
iast: yastvātmaratireva syādātmatṛptaśca mānavaḥ · ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṁ na vidyate
meaning: But for one who delights in the Self, is satisfied in the Self and content in the Self alone, there is no duty left to do.
lifeNote: Inner contentment frees you from the restless need to prove yourself.
actions: Spend ten minutes today doing nothing but enjoying being alive.
Notice one thing you do only to prove yourself, and let it go once.
Write down three things you like about who you are.

iast: naiva tasya kṛtenārtho nākṛteneha kaścana · na cāsya sarvabhūteṣu kaścidarthavyapāśrayaḥ
meaning: Such a person has nothing to gain by acting and nothing to lose by not acting, and depends on no being for anything.
lifeNote: Freedom is needing nothing from others to feel whole.
actions: Do something kind today without needing anything back.
Notice one way you depend on approval, and loosen it.
Enjoy an activity today just for itself.

iast: tasmādasaktaḥ satataṁ kāryaṁ karma samācara · asakto hyācarankarma paramāpnoti pūruṣaḥ
meaning: Therefore always do the work that must be done, without attachment. By working without attachment, a person reaches the Supreme.
lifeNote: Do what needs doing, and let it go. That is the whole of Karma Yoga in one line.
actions: Finish one necessary task today and do not dwell on it afterwards.
Write "do it, then let it go" on a note near your desk.
Help with a chore at home without being asked.

iast: karmaṇaiva hi saṁsiddhimāsthitā janakādayaḥ · lokasaṁgrahamevāpi saṁpaśyankartumarhasi
meaning: Kings like Janaka reached perfection through action alone. Even for the sake of guiding the world, you should act.
lifeNote: Even if you do not need anything, others learn from how you act. Lead by example.
actions: Do your work today knowing someone may be learning from you.
Mentor someone younger in a small way this week.
Set a good example in one habit at home.

iast: yadyadācarati śreṣṭhastattadevetaro janaḥ · sa yatpramāṇaṁ kurute lokastadanuvartate
meaning: Whatever a great person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world follows.
lifeNote: People copy what you do more than what you say. Be the example you want to see.
actions: Do one thing today that you would want a child to copy.
Keep a standard at work even when no one checks.
Notice who looks up to you and act with that in mind.

sanskrit: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन ।
iast: na me pārthāsti kartavyaṁ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana · nānavāptamavāptavyaṁ varta eva ca karmaṇi
meaning: Arjuna, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, nothing I lack or need to gain; yet I keep on acting.
lifeNote: Krishna works not because he must but because it helps others. Purpose can outlast need.
actions: Do one helpful thing today that you do not need to do.
Keep going on a good habit even after you have reached your goal.
Help a colleague finish their work after yours is done.

sanskrit: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः ।
iast: yadi hyahaṁ na varteyaṁ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ · mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ
meaning: If I ever stopped working tirelessly, Arjuna, people everywhere would follow my example.
lifeNote: Others are watching how you show up. Your effort quietly lifts people around you.
actions: Show up fully for one commitment today.
Notice how others respond when you bring energy to a task.
Avoid one shortcut today because someone may copy it.

sanskrit: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् ।
iast: utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṁ karma cedaham · saṅkarasya ca kartā syāmupahanyāmimāḥ prajāḥ
meaning: If I did not act, these worlds would fall into ruin. I would cause confusion and the destruction of these beings.
lifeNote: Your work holds up more than you realise. Do not underestimate what your effort keeps going.
actions: Notice who depends on the work you do and thank them for trusting you.
Do one routine duty today with full care.
Write down what would fall apart if you stopped one of your responsibilities.

iast: saktāḥ karmaṇyavidvāṁso yathā kurvanti bhārata · kuryādvidvāṁstathāsaktaścikīrṣurlokasaṁgraham
